title: 「食料品の消費税ゼロ」高市首相は断行できるか、政権が複数吹っ飛んだ政治銘柄　平井文夫
extracted_text: 消費税は日本では「政治銘柄」と呼ばれ、これまで「増税」でいくつも政権が吹っ飛んだ。1989年に最初に3％を導入した竹下登首相は不祥事も加わり2カ月後に退陣。97年に5％に上げた橋本龍太郎首相は経済低迷で翌年の参院選に大敗し、この人も退陣した。 2014年に8％に上げた安倍晋三首相は3人の中では最も政権基盤が強かったが、それでも消費の落ち込みを受けて10％への引き上げを2度延期せざるを得なかった。 そして、「与党が増税し、野党が減税を主張する」という構図が続いてきたのだが、ここにきて少し変化が見えている。 まず中道改革連合の階猛幹事長は先月19日、衆院選で掲げた「恒久的な食料品消費税ゼロ」について「難しい」との認識を示した。 これに対し、小川淳也代表が同24日、「今後も公約として消費減税を掲げる」と述べて階氏の発言を打ち消した。階氏は「難しい」理由について、「恒久財源を見つけるのは正直言って自信がない」と語っている。
translated_text: In Japan, consumption tax is called a 'political issue,' and up to now, tax increases have caused several administrations to fall. Prime Minister Noboru Takeshita, who first introduced the 3% tax in 1989, resigned just two months later amid scandals. Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who raised it to 5% in 1997, suffered a major defeat in the following year's Upper House election due to economic stagnation and also resigned. Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who raised it to 8% in 2014, had the strongest political base of the three, but even he was forced to postpone the increase to 10% twice due to the decline in consumer spending. And the pattern of 'the ruling party advocating tax increases while the opposition calls for tax cuts' has continued, but recently some changes have become apparent. First, Coalition for Reform from the Center's Secretary-General Hashiru Takai expressed last month that implementing 'permanent zero consumption tax on food' promised in the Lower House election would be 'difficult.' In response, Representative Jun Ogawa stated on the 24th that they would 'continue to include consumption tax reduction in their policy platform,' countering Takai's statement. Regarding why it's 'difficult,' Takai said, 'To be honest, I'm not confident we can find a permanent funding source.'
title_en: "Zero Food Consumption Tax" - Can Prime Minister Takashi Actually Implement It? The Political Issue That Has Toppled Multiple Administrations
